finding.claim: POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban runs do_ban for any caller whose g.user is not an admin, because the 403 from require_admin is swallowed by a broad except and the ban proceeds.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled <uid> path segment, plus any authenticated session whose g.user dict has a falsy is_admin (admin.py:17 precondition).
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a protected administrative operation.

trace.note: Route POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban; uid comes from the URL.
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block.
For a non-admin, abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, a subclass of Exception.
except Exception catches the Forbidden, so the 403 never reaches the client.
Only a warning is logged, including g.user.get('name').
Execution falls through and do_ban(uid) runs with no admin check.
Response is {ok: true}, so the non-admin caller sees success.

finding.guards_checked: Checked: require_admin at admin.py:9-11 is correct but its failure is swallowed by the caller. The try/except at admin.py:16-19 is the defect: it catches Exception, which includes HTTP 403 aborts, and continues. No decorators, before_request hooks, or blueprint auth exist in admin.py; any such control would live outside this file and was not verified. unban at admin.py:24-28 is correct and calls require_admin without a try block, showing the intended behaviour. No uid validation exists; do_ban is a stub here, so real impact depends on its implementation.
finding.repro: Log in as a non-admin user and POST /admin/users/<victim_uid>/ban. Expected 403; actual 200 {"ok": true} with do_ban(<victim_uid>) executed. Assumes the auth layer sets g.user to a dict with is_admin false. If g.user is unset, line 19 raises AttributeError inside the except block, giving a 500 and no ban.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does abort(403), but its call at admin.py:17 sits inside try, and except Exception at admin.py:18 swallows the werkzeug Forbidden (an Exception subclass). Execution then reaches do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 and returns ok=true at admin.py:21. The unban route at admin.py:26 calls require_admin without a try block, which shows the intended behaviour. The repo has no other auth code: admin.py is the only code file, with no before_request hook or decorator. The auth layer that sets g.user is not in the repo and is assumed to yield a dict with a falsy is_admin for non-admins.
verdict.reason: The trace matches admin.py:14-21: require_admin's abort(403) at admin.py:11 is raised inside the try at admin.py:16-19, the bare except at admin.py:18 swallows it, and do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any non-admin authenticated caller, so the candidate's claim holds as stated. Real impact depends on do_ban, which is a stub at admin.py:31-32.
